headline: Nicolas Cage says he refused to sign an AI waiver for Amazon’s “Spider-Noir” series and will probably not work with the studio again.
score_reason: VIRAL RULE (CLAUDE.md): carried by 36 distinct outlets in the window, so the score is at least 7; the writer had lowered it to 6 because the waiver claim is Cage’s alone and Amazon is not quoted. That doubt stays in the status REPORTED and the summary.
importance_line: A leading actor publicly says he turned down an AI waiver and may stop working with a major studio, which matters to performers first, then studios that ask actors to consent to AI use, but it is Cage’s own account and Amazon has not been quoted.
summary: Variety reports that Nicolas Cage told a New York Comic Con panel on Saturday that he refused to sign a waiver allowing AI use on “Spider-Noir”, which Amazon allegedly asked of him, saying “I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s okay.” Amazon dropped the Prime Video superhero series last month after one season, shortly before the Emmys, where it was up for 11 awards, and Variety carries no Amazon response, so the waiver claim rests on Cage’s account.
notes: Full Variety text read. Cage also said his next project is HBO’s True Detective; HBO had not confirmed (left out of the summary).
